description.narrative: Africa Rural Climate Adaptation Finance Mechanism Uganda (ARCAFIM Uganda) is an initiative led by the International Fund for Agriculture Development (IFAD) to bridge the gap between global and regional climate financing and the local needs for adaptation investment in Uganda. Through the Uganda country office, the contribution supports ARCAFIM’s work in Uganda and focuses on mobilising international financing for adaptation through key soft components, like linking funders and financial institutions, ensuring the use of international standards and working with producers and farmers, including women-led farms and enterprises.

actual.value: Joint Equity Bank and IFAD field missions to Equity Bank branches in all targeted countries in East Africa were conducted. Practical adjustments were identified and proposed for informing fast CCA portfolio development in Equity Bank as well as development of appropriate CCA products for ARCAFIM implementation particularly in Uganda. Among the proposals made were on Equity bank smallholder lending concerning more appropriate policies on maximum loan amounts, alternative loan collaterals and the financing structures of the loan packages. However, undertaking this type of innovative adjustments to the ARCAFIM products and organizing effective awareness creation, training, and marketing campaigns in targeted rural areas will be of key importance for reaching the planned outreach and impact with this large-scale CCA financing initiative.

actual.value:
Building on the CCA taxonomy developed during the ARCAFIM pilot, the project participated in the Technical Working Committee for the Uganda National Green Taxonomy ensuring successful integration of ARCAFIM taxonomy into the Uganda National Green Finance Taxonomy. This alignment aimed at strengthening the enabling environment for climate adaptation finance by providing a standardized framework for financial institutions to assess and invest in climate resilient projects.
A national consultant procured who supported initial activities towards climate finance mobilization efforts in Uganda by engaging in strategic policy and knowledge initiatives that lay the foundation for institutional adoption of climate adaptation finance solutions. The consultant coordinated with the Frankfurt School of Finance and Managements on designing the climate adaptation finance course, actively engaged stakeholders in the climate and CCA finance sectors in Uganda at workshops, events and engaged existing projects, including those by Denmark, GCF etc to explore build synergies and share experiences.
In partnership with the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management, the first cohort for climate adaptation finance training was launched in December 2024 with an enrolment of 18 financial sector professionals.

actual.value: In partnership with the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management and together with MUBS, the project continued to deliver the second cohort of the Climate Change Adaptation Finance course for Financial Sector Managers and Specialists. The course was opened up to cover all East African countries targeted by the regional ARCAFIM. A total of 47 professionals out of the targeted 80 completed the ARCAFIM course.

actual.value:
Building onto the gender analysis completed in 2024, the project finalised the Gender Strategy and Action Plan, Gender Capacity Building Plan and Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) framework for the gender strategy and action plan.
A Climate Finance Brief on the Status of Climate Change Adaptation Financing in Rural and Agricultural Sector in Uganda was successfully developed.
ARCAFIM Uganda supported and participated in the Second Annual Climate Finance Conference hosted by Makerere University Business School (MUBS) and Uganda Institute of Banking and Financial Services (UIBFS) in April 2025. Specifically, ARCAFIM participated in a panel discussion co hosted with the Danish Embassy and, focused on climate adaptation finance and the role of private sector engagement.
Successful inception review of ARCAFIM by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) of Denmark.
The monitoring and evaluation (M&E) specialist recruited in 2025 commenced the task of building ARCAFIM Uganda results framework, monitoring system, and impact assessment methodologies. This assignment is still ongoing as of early 2026.
Recruitment of the Climate Finance Specialist was completed in August 2025. The approved national (NOB) Climate Finance Officer position has also been successfully filled by an IFAD internal staff at the Uganda country office whereas, the recruitment of the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) to is ongoing.

target.value: Project document form the basis for the implementation.

actual.value:
Experts to support various aspects of the project including the Gender and climate finance analyses as well as an Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist were successfully hired. However, while development of ToRs have been completed, recruitment of the Senior Climate Finance Specialist is yet to be concluded. Similarly, ToRs for the JPO (to be funded by Denmark) and the National Climate Finance Officer were developed however, their recruitment is yet to start.
A Gender Analysis was completed, with the Gender Action Plan has been drafted to be completed in 2025. The gender analysis assessed the existing gender dynamics within rural finance and agriculture sectors in Uganda and, focused on structural barriers to accessing climate adaptation finance for women youth and other vulnerable groups.
A draft strategic assessment of climate finance landscape in Uganda was completed. The report entails a baseline financial flow analysis, stakeholder engagement insights, and policy recommendations. Its validation is planned for early February 2025 with a completed report to developed into a climate finance policy brief.
